- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot in the short term.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative or shows recent downward momentum.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment turns sharply positive, model delays the price rise, underestimating the peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overcorrects after sharp spikes, leading to premature declines.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the first 7–10 days of the 30-day horizon; adjust downward for early periods.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model tends to average out extremes, missing sharp directional moves.
- Avoid over-relying on recent sentiment; sentiment history should be weighted more heavily for 3–5 day windows to capture momentum.
